mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% over two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing industrial production (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market signals (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which reduces related corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining housing starts (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under a tight monetary policy, which increases costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high inflation under tight monetary policy (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing retail sales (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
